messages:
alex_dev: Heads up — AcmeCorp support ticket reporting a spike of 502/504 + client timeouts starting ~02:15 UTC. They say it's affecting their checkout flow (high QPS). Support attached a sample request_id list and a short trace.

priya_support: FYI they saw ~60 errors over 10m, most are `504 gateway timeout` from our edge. Customer also reported an unexpected billing spike correlated with retries. Ticket: #AC-4491.

jordan_ops: Can someone paste a couple request_ids and the raw gateway logs? I want to see upstream latency and whether auth proxy is involved.

priya_support: Request IDs: `r-20260317-0a1b2c3d`, `r-20260317-0a1b2c3e`, `r-20260317-0a1b2c3f`. Customer curl: `curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-medium","inputs":"<payload>","max_tokens":1024}'`

alex_dev: Pasted a couple logs into thread: `edge.gateway: upstream timeout after 30s, code=504, upstream=hosted-inference-prod-us-west-2`. Also see `authz: token validation slow (p95 420ms)`, but nothing catastrophic there.

mike_sre: Seeing correlated signs on the proxy pool: a small subset of auth-proxy pods hit CPU steal + network retransmits ~02:12-02:22. KV cache miss rate spiked for that customer (prefix caching not working), which increased backend load.

jordan_ops: Repro steps requested. priya, did support run a local repro with the same token/header? If customer is retrying aggressively on 30s client timeout that could create a retry storm and billing spike.

priya_support: Customer provided sample repro script — we validated locally against staging and saw 1/10 requests time out with similar error. They used `concurrency=8` and `payload ~ 1.2MB` (long context + attachments).

mike_sre: Actionable short-term mitigation: 1) enable temporary rate-limiting on that route for the customer (limit concurrency to 4) 2) bump frontend timeout to 45s as a holding measure 3) route failing requests to a cheaper, lower-latency model variant for retries. Can someone take those?

jordan_ops: I'll pivot the rate-limit and timeout patch (edge config). Patching now to limit to 4 concurrent requests for AcmeCorp. Will monitor p95.

alex_dev: I'll implement a model-fallback rule in routing to prefer `gpt-medium-legacy` on retry for this customer. That should reduce backend tail latency while preserving success rate.

sabrina_pm: Also need comms: Priya, coordinate an update to AcmeCorp explaining we're throttling to mitigate immediate impact and we'll follow with a root-cause postmortem.

priya_support: On it. I'll send a status note + temporary workaround docs.

mike_sre: Long-term follow-ups (assign): - Investigate auth-proxy CPU/retx root cause (owner: @mike_sre) - Fix prefix/KV caching regression for certain payload patterns (owner: @alex_dev) - Eval retry/backoff guidance in SDKs and add server-side safe-retries policy (owner: @sabrina_pm) - Billing anomaly check (owner: @priya_support with finance)

alex_dev: Noted. I'll open GH issues with links to logs and include a small reproducer from the customer's payload.

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-17-ACME-504. Severity: P2. War room channel: #inc-5943219876 (private).

priya_support: Quick follow-up: Customer confirmed partial recovery after we applied rate-limit + fallback. They still want a postmortem and clarity on how to avoid billing spikes. Scheduling sync for 10:00 UTC.

jordan_ops: Monitoring dashboard shows p95 latency dropping to normal in 15m after the change. Will keep watch for 1h and then propose rollback of aggressive mitigations if stable. :thumbsup:

mike_sre: Saving logs and traces to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/5943219876/logs.tar.gz. I'll include sampling of slow traces and auth-proxy metrics.

sabrina_pm: Great. Priya please include next steps and ETA for RCA in the customer note. We'll convert the GH issues into a formal postmortem template once we have root causes.

priya_support: Will do. Closing immediate support handoff. Recording action items in the incident.

alex_dev: Thanks everyone. Leaving the channel open for any late regressions.
